title: 4. The human tip: a managed layer when it is worth it

sections.name: summary
sections.label: In short
sections.content: A strongly managed human layer is right for some things, some of the time; work should not depend on it.

sections.name: body
sections.label: The evidence
sections.content: The owner, 2026-10-30: "There is room for a purely human controlled affirmation layer, but we should be able to work without it ... Sometimes I might start there, sometimes it might get there eventually. But we don't always need it." The affirmation layer chapter of the clerk handbook already puts it beside the flow, never a step in it, from vignette 81f2bf49: "I have to say yes because I assume it's right... The very thing that was supposed to be the sovereign anchor becomes exactly the thing that undermines it." Remedy 2910ac1e (affirm in context, srs-web#617) puts a tick or deny where the owner writes (67459d40). Decision c373c2c1 refuses any change that affirms or ratifies on the owner's behalf. The owner also wants some things fixed: "Our chat sourced axes stay affirmed" (a5a9c651), affirmation steps belong to the holon setup (e51415f2), and an affirmed remedy is still only a hypothesis (2941f51a).

sections.name: open
sections.label: Open
sections.content: Which kinds of record start at the tip (axes, decisions, the purpose), which may rise to it, and which never need it?
